I1.quote: The adsorption of H2 on CG-CMs at 77 K and up to 1 bar was analyzed using a volumetric adsorption analyzer.

I2.quote: The carbon monoliths were prepared by compressing the mixture of corn grain-based activated carbons and sodium derived carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt.

I3.quote: In overall, the maximum hydrogen uptake on three different carbon monoliths was observed in between 2.39–2.45 wt% at 77 K and 1 bar.
I3.location: main, p. 3 (journal p. 236), Section 3.2 (data in Fig. 3)

I5.quote: The hydrogen (H2) adsorption capacity of the highly porous novel corn grain-based carbon monoliths (CG-CMs) was assessed.

notes: Original research article. H2 uptake measured on the same three carbon monoliths (MR-1/2, MR-1/3, MR-1/4) volumetrically at 77 K up to 1 bar (Fig. 3) and gravimetrically (Rubotherm magnetic suspension microbalance) at 298 K up to 50 bar (Fig. 5; 0.40, 0.41, 0.46 wt% at 298 K and 50 bar, Section 3.3). The paper states 'this is the first report about the adsorption of hydrogen on CG-CMs' (Section 2.1), so duplicate_data does not apply; the N2 isotherms are cited from ref. [18] but the H2 data are new. The monolith binder (carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt) is a minor component; the sorbent is activated-carbon based. Not retracted per record.json and no retraction notice in the PDF.
